775	relative functorial action): if `L ~ L'` via the coset witness `N`, then
776	`g_C^* L ~ g_C^* L'` via the coset witness `g^* N`. The iso chain is
777	`g_C^* L ≅ g_C^*(π_T^* N ⊗ L') ≅ g_C^* π_T^* N ⊗ g_C^* L'
778	≅ π_{T'}^*(g^* N) ⊗ g_C^* L'` (functoriality,
779	`pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial`, `pullback_pullback_eq`). -/
780	theorem relPicRel_pullback {S C T T' : Scheme.{u}}
781	    {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S} {πT' : T' ⟶ S} {g : T' ⟶ T}
782	    {hg : πT' = g ≫ πT} {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT}
783	    (h : relPicRel πC πT L L') :
784	    relPicRel πC πT'
785	      ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullback (baseChangeOverC πC πT πT' g hg)).obj L.carrier,
786	        L.isLocallyTrivial.pullback _⟩
787	      ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullback (baseChangeOverC πC πT πT' g hg)).obj L'.carrier,
788	        L'.isLocallyTrivial.pullback _⟩ := by
789	  obtain ⟨N, hN, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
790	  refine ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N, hN.pullback g, ⟨?_⟩⟩
791	  refine (Scheme.Modules.pullback (baseChangeOverC πC πT πT' g hg)).mapIso e ≪≫ ?_
792	  refine Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial _ _ _
793	    (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).isLocallyTrivial
794	    L'.isLocallyTrivial ≪≫ ?_
795	  exact Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
796	    (LineBundle.pullback_pullback_eq πC πT πT' g hg N).some (Iso.refl _)
797	
798	/-- **Functoriality on the RELATIVE `H_T`-quotient, group-hom form**
799	(blueprint `lem:rel_pic_sharp_functorial`, honest relative carrier). For a
800	test morphism `g : T' ⟶ T` over `S`, the pullback `[L] ↦ [g_C^* L]` descends
801	to the `H_T`-coset quotients (`relPicRel_pullback`) and is a group
802	homomorphism (structure-sheaf and tensor preservation, exactly as in the
803	absolute `functorial`). -/
804	noncomputable def relFunctorial {S C T T' : Scheme.{u}}
805	    (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) (πT' : T' ⟶ S) (g : T' ⟶ T)
806	    (hg : πT' = g ≫ πT) :
807	    Quotient (relPicSetoid πC πT) →+ Quotient (relPicSetoid πC πT') where
808	  toFun := Quotient.lift
809	    (fun L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT =>
810	      Quotient.mk (relPicSetoid πC πT')
811	        (⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullback (baseChangeOverC πC πT πT' g hg)).obj L.carrier,
812	          L.isLocallyTrivial.pullback _⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT'))
813	    (fun _ _ h => Quotient.sound (relPicRel_pullback h))
814	  map_zero' := Quotient.sound (relPicRel_of_iso ⟨Modules.pullbackUnitIso _⟩)
815	  map_add' a b := by
816	    induction a using Quotient.ind with | _ L => ?_
817	    induction b using Quotient.ind with | _ L' => ?_
818	    exact Quotient.sound (relPicRel_of_iso
819	      ⟨Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial _ L.carrier L'.carrier
820	        L.isLocallyTrivial L'.isLocallyTrivial⟩)
821	
822	/-- `relFunctorial` at the identity is the identity (`pullback.map_id` +
823	`Modules.pullbackId` descended through the `H_T`-quotient). -/
824	private lemma relFunctorial_id {S C T : Scheme.{u}}
825	    (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) (hg : πT = 𝟙 T ≫ πT)
826	    (a : Quotient (relPicSetoid πC πT)) :
827	    relFunctorial πC πT πT (𝟙 T) hg a = a := by
828	  induction a using Quotient.ind with | _ L => ?_
829	  refine Quotient.sound (relPicRel_of_iso
830	    ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr ?_).app L.carrier ≪≫
831	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId _).app L.carrier⟩)
832	  apply Limits.pullback.hom_ext <;> simp [baseChangeOverC]
833	
834	/-- `relFunctorial` is contravariantly compositional (`pullback.hom_ext`
835	chase + `Modules.pullbackComp` descended through the `H_T`-quotient). -/
836	private lemma relFunctorial_comp {S C T T' T'' : Scheme.{u}}
837	    (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) (πT' : T' ⟶ S) (πT'' : T'' ⟶ S)
838	    (g : T' ⟶ T) (h : T'' ⟶ T') (hg : πT' = g ≫ πT) (hh : πT'' = h ≫ πT')
839	    (hgh : πT'' = (h ≫ g) ≫ πT)
840	    (a : Quotient (relPicSetoid πC πT)) :
841	    relFunctorial πC πT πT'' (h ≫ g) hgh a
842	      = relFunctorial πC πT' πT'' h hh (relFunctorial πC πT πT' g hg a) := by
843	  induction a using Quotient.ind with | _ L => ?_
844	  refine Quotient.sound (relPicRel_of_iso
845	    ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr ?_).app L.carrier ≪≫
846	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp _ _).symm.app L.carrier⟩)
847	  apply Limits.pullback.hom_ext <;>
848	    simp [baseChangeOverC, Limits.pullback.lift_fst, Limits.pullback.lift_snd,
849	      Limits.pullback.lift_snd_assoc]
850	
851	/-- **The RELATIVE Picard presheaf** `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` as a
852	group-valued functor — the Kleiman `df:Pfs` object, on the
853	`H_T`-coset carrier `Quotient (relPicSetoid _C.hom T.unop.hom)` with the
854	group structure `addCommGroup_via_tensorObj` and the pullback-descended
855	morphism action `relFunctorial`. The absolute functor `PicSharp` above
856	compares onto it via the quotient map `toRelPresheaf`. -/
857	noncomputable def relPresheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (_C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
858	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 _C.hom] [IsProper _C.hom] :
859	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} where
860	  obj T := AddCommGrpCat.of (Quotient (relPicSetoid _C.hom T.unop.hom))
861	  map {T T'} g := AddCommGrpCat.ofHom
862	    (relFunctorial _C.hom T.unop.hom T'.unop.hom g.unop.left (Over.w g.unop).symm)
863	  map_id T := by
864	    ext a
865	    exact relFunctorial_id _C.hom T.unop.hom _ a
866	  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
867	    ext a
868	    exact relFunctorial_comp _C.hom T.unop.hom T'.unop.hom T''.unop.hom
869	      g.unop.left h.unop.left (Over.w g.unop).symm (Over.w h.unop).symm _ a
870	
871	/-- **The quotient comparison** `Pic(C ×_k T) ⟶ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`,
872	natural in `T`: the componentwise `H_T`-coset quotient map from the absolute
873	functor `PicSharp` to the relative functor `relPresheaf` (a group
874	homomorphism because the group laws on both sides descend the same tensor
875	operations; the `H_T`-relation is coarser than the iso-class relation by
876	`relPicRel_of_iso`). -/
877	noncomputable def toRelPresheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (_C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
878	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 _C.hom] [IsProper _C.hom] :
879	    PicSharp _C ⟶ relPresheaf _C where
880	  app T := AddCommGrpCat.ofHom
881	    { toFun := Quotient.lift
882	        (fun L => Quotient.mk (relPicSetoid _C.hom T.unop.hom) L)
883	        (fun _ _ e => Quotient.sound (relPicRel_of_iso e))
884	      map_zero' := rfl
885	      map_add' := by
886	        rintro ⟨a⟩ ⟨b⟩
887	        rfl }
888	  naturality {T T'} g := by
889	    ext a
890	    induction a using Quotient.ind with | _ L => ?_
891	    rfl
892	
893	end PicSharp
894	
895	/-! ## §5. Étale sheafification
896	
897	The relative Picard presheaf `PicSharp_{C/k}` is not *a priori* a sheaf
898	(Kleiman §2, L1330), and over a general field it is **not representable**:
899	Kleiman L5105–L5108 states this for the conic `u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, a smooth
900	plane conic and hence smooth, proper and geometrically integral over a field with
901	no rational point. In Lean that step is
902	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
903	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`), whose one open input is that the comparison
904	really fails for that conic.
905	
906	(**Two citations have been wrong in this slot, both corrected 2026-07-29.** "§2
907	L1292–L1302", which stood here for weeks, is about the *absolute* functor
908	`Pic_X` — the relative one quotients by `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that
909	argument. Its first replacement, `ex:Pfs`, compares the two *sheafifications*, so
910	it does not show `picSharp` failing Zariski descent either; `th:cmp` part 1 in
911	fact gives `picSharp ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` here. Do not rebuild the argument through
912	a sheaf condition. Full account in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`'s module
913	docstring.)
914	
915	To obtain a representable
916	functor in the sense of `chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability`, one
917	replaces `PicSharp_{C/k}` by its **associated étale sheaf**
918	`Pic^♯_{(C/k)ét} := (PicSharp_{C/k})^{∼ét}`. Kleiman §4
919	(Theorem `th:main`) represents precisely this sheafified functor.
920	
921	The sheafification is encoded as `presheafToSheaf J _` applied to the
922	bundled `PicSharp.presheaf`, for a **parameter** Grothendieck topology
923	`J` on `Over (Spec k)`, because Mathlib does not ship an étale
924	Grothendieck topology on schemes (only the morphism property
925	`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`); `J` is to be bound to the canonical étale
926	topology once that is available.
927	
928	*Naming note*: the blueprint pins this declaration under
929	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme`, which already names the
930	*representing scheme* in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, so the
931	namespaced name `PicSharp.etSheaf` is used here instead.
932	
933	Blueprint reference: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification` (Kleiman §2,
934	`df:Pfs` étale-sheaf clause). -/
935	
936	/-- The **étale sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf**.
937	
938	Given a smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C` over a field
939	`k`, and a Grothendieck topology `J` on `Over (Spec k)` (intended: the
940	canonical étale topology on `(Sch/k)`), the **étale-sheafified relative
941	Picard functor**
942	
943	```
944	Pic^♯_{(C/k)ét} := (PicSharp_{C/k})^{~_ét}
945	```
946	
947	is the sheafification of the group-valued presheaf
948	`PicSharp.presheaf` of `thm:rel_pic_sharp_presheaf`. Equivalently, it is
949	the unique (up to canonical isomorphism) sheaf of abelian groups on the
950	site `(Over (Spec k), J)` equipped with a presheaf morphism
951	`PicSharp.presheaf ⟶ (forget _) ∘ -` universal among presheaf morphisms
952	to abelian-group sheaves.
953

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StructureSheafPushforward
9	
10	/-!
11	# Rigidified relative Picard bundles (B1: the `RigidifiedPic` API)
12	
13	For a relative curve `πC : C ⟶ S` with a **section of the projection**
14	`σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` (i.e. `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`, where `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`), Kleiman's
15	rigidification of the relative Picard functor replaces a bare line bundle `L` on
16	`C ×_S T` by a *rigidified* one — a bundle equipped with a trivialisation of its
17	restriction `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T` along the section. Rigidified bundles have no non-trivial
18	automorphisms (`lm:aut`, the ring-level heart of which is
19	`StructureSheafPushforward.eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one_of_gate`), so the
20	rigidified functor is a Zariski sheaf and represents the relative Picard functor.
21	
22	This file supplies the substrate of that programme:
23	
24	* `sectionPullbackProjIso` — the section base-change iso `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N` (from
25	  `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T` via the pullback pseudofunctor);
26	* `Rigidification σ L` — a trivialisation `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`;
27	* `exists_rigidification_relPicRel` — **Kleiman `lm:fff`**: every `L` is
28	  `H_T`-equivalent to a rigidified bundle `L' = L ⊗ π_T^*((σ^* L)⁻¹)`;
29	* `rationalPointSection` — the section `σ_T` of the projection produced by a
30	  `k`-rational point `x₀` of `C`, matching the hypothesis shape consumed by the
31	  `StructureSheafPushforward` `lm:aut` lemmas.
32	
33	Blueprint references: Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, Lemmas `lm:fff` (existence of the
34	rigidified representative), `lm:aut` (automorphism-freeness). The `H_T`-relation
35	`PicSharp.relPicRel` is the one of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean`.
36	-/
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Limits
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	namespace Scheme
45	
46	namespace PicSharp
47	
48	/-! ## §1. The section base-change isomorphism -/
49	
50	/-- **Section base-change iso** `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N`.
51	
52	For a section `σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` of the projection `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`
53	(so `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`) and a sheaf of modules `N` on `T`, the pullback pseudofunctor
54	identity `(σ ≫ π_T)^* ≅ σ^* ∘ π_T^*` together with `𝟙_T^* ≅ id` identifies the
55	double pullback `σ^*(π_T^* N)` with `N`. This is the same three-step
56	`pullbackComp`/`pullbackCongr`/`pullbackId` chain as `LineBundle.pullback_pullback_eq`,
57	specialised to a section. -/
58	noncomputable def sectionPullbackProjIso {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
59	    (σ : T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT)

67

71	    (σ : T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT) (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) where
72	  /-- The trivialising isomorphism `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`. -/
73	  triv : (Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj L.carrier ≅ SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf
74

77	/-- **Existence of a rigidified representative** (Kleiman §2, `lm:fff`).
78	
79	Every line bundle `L` on `C ×_S T` is `H_T`-equivalent (`PicSharp.relPicRel`) to a
80	line bundle `L'` carrying a rigidification along the section `σ`. Explicitly
81	`L' = L ⊗ π_T^*((σ^* L)⁻¹)`: its restriction along `σ` is
82	`σ^*L ⊗ σ^*(π_T^*(σ^*L)⁻¹) ≅ σ^*L ⊗ (σ^*L)⁻¹ ≅ 𝒪_T`
83	(using the section base-change iso `sectionPullbackProjIso`), and `L' ≅ π_T^*((σ^*L)⁻¹) ⊗ L`
84	differs from `L` by a pullback from the base, hence `[L'] = [L]` in
85	`Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`. -/
86	theorem exists_rigidification_relPicRel {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
87	    (σ : T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT)
88	    (hσ : σ ≫ Limits.pullback.snd πC πT = 𝟙 T) (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) :
89	    ∃ L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT,
90	      Nonempty (Rigidification σ L') ∧ PicSharp.relPicRel πC πT L' L := by
91	  classical
92	  -- `σ^* L` is locally trivial (pullback of a line bundle is a line bundle, 01HH).
93	  have hσL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial ((Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj L.carrier) :=
94	    L.isLocallyTrivial.pullback σ
95	  -- Its tensor inverse `Ninv` on `T`, with `eN : σ^* L ⊗ Ninv ≅ 𝒪_T`.
96	  obtain ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨eN⟩⟩ := Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse hσL
97	  -- The twist `L' := L ⊗ π_T^* Ninv`.
98	  refine ⟨⟨Modules.tensorObj L.carrier
99	      (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier,
100	      Modules.tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial L.isLocallyTrivial
101	        (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).isLocallyTrivial⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
102	  · -- Rigidification of `L'`:
103	    -- `σ^*(L ⊗ π_T^*Ninv) ≅ σ^*L ⊗ σ^*(π_T^*Ninv) ≅ σ^*L ⊗ Ninv ≅ 𝒪_T`.
104	    exact ⟨⟨Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial σ L.carrier
105	          (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier
106	          L.isLocallyTrivial
107	          (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).isLocallyTrivial ≪≫
108	        Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) (sectionPullbackProjIso σ hσ Ninv) ≪≫ eN⟩⟩
109	  · -- `H_T`-equivalence `L' ~ L`: `L' = L ⊗ π_T^*Ninv ≅ π_T^*Ninv ⊗ L` (braiding), take `N = Ninv`.
110	    exact ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨Modules.tensorObj_braiding L.carrier
111	      (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier⟩⟩
112

114	
115	/-- **The section of the projection produced by a rational point.** A `k`-rational

117	test object `T` with structure map `πT : T ⟶ S`, a section
118	`σ_T := ⟨π_T ≫ x₀, 𝟙_T⟩ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` of the projection `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`.
119	This is the section along which the relative Picard functor is rigidified. -/
120	noncomputable def rationalPointSection {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} (πT : T ⟶ S)
121	    (x₀ : S ⟶ C) (hx₀ : x₀ ≫ πC = 𝟙 S) :
122	    T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT :=
123	  Limits.pullback.lift (πT ≫ x₀) (𝟙 T)
124	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hx₀, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp])
125	
126	@[simp]
127	theorem rationalPointSection_comp_snd {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} (πT : T ⟶ S)
128	    (x₀ : S ⟶ C) (hx₀ : x₀ ≫ πC = 𝟙 S) :
129	    rationalPointSection πT x₀ hx₀ ≫ Limits.pullback.snd πC πT = 𝟙 T :=
130	  Limits.pullback.lift_snd _ _ _

9	/-!
10	# Subcanonicity of the étale site, and the section-free transport `picSharp → picEt`
11	
12	This file settles a **route** question about the project's central obligation
13	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), and
14	it settles it in the direction opposite to what that file's docstring and the
15	board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep` currently assert.
16	
17	## The claim this file refutes
18	
19	Clause (1) of the seam asks for representability of the étale-sheafified
20	functor `PicScheme.picEt C`, while every milestone of the Milne–Kollár campaign
21	targets the *unsheafified* `PicScheme.picSharp C`. The seam docstring and the
22	board row both say the gap between them **cannot be bridged without a
23	`k`-rational point**, on the grounds that the comparison
24	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 — an isomorphism only under
25	a section — and that a section is exactly what the owner decision `I-0491`
26	forbids the headline to carry.
27	
28	That reasoning is wrong, and the error is a direction confusion. Kleiman §2
29	Thm 2.5 is the statement that a section makes the comparison an isomorphism
30	*with no hypothesis on the presheaf*. But there is a second, entirely
31	independent, route to the same conclusion: the comparison is the sheafification
32	unit, and a unit is an isomorphism **exactly when its source is already a
33	sheaf** (`CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify`). A representable functor is a sheaf
34	for any subcanonical topology. So *if* the campaign delivers representability of
35	`picSharp`, the source is a sheaf for that reason alone, the unit is an
36	isomorphism, and no section is involved anywhere.
37	
38	The consequence for the route, stated precisely because the board row is
39	currently priced on its negation: the campaign's endpoint **is** transportable
40	to clause (1). `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` below is that
41	transport, proved with no rational-point hypothesis of any kind.
42	
43	## What is actually still open
44	
45	This file does **not** close the seam. It removes an alleged obstruction, which
46	is a different thing, and the honest statement of what remains is:
47	
48	* the antecedent of every theorem here is representability of `picSharp C`
49	  over an arbitrary field — campaign milestones J1–J5, G3, G4, B1/B4/B6,
50	  D2′–D4′, P5 — and **not one of those is discharged**. No theorem in this file
51	  is applied to a curve anywhere in the project, and none should be reported as
52	  progress on the existence question;
53	* what changes is the *shape* of the remaining work. Before this file, a reader
54	  of the seam docstring concluded that finishing the campaign leaves a further
55	  unpriced obligation ("represent `picEt` directly, or restate the headline").
56	  After it, no supplementary étale-representability theorem is needed: `picEt`
57	  representability follows from `picSharp` representability by `Subcanonical` +
58	  `isIso_toSheafify`, both already in Mathlib.
59	
60	**But the antecedent must not be read as reachable over `k`, and §4 is why.**
61	The same subcanonicity that powers the transport also proves that a
62	representable `picSharp` is a *Zariski* sheaf
63	(`PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`).
64	
65	**But the falsity of `picSharp` representability is quoted from Kleiman, NOT
66	derived from that theorem** — corrected 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc` / `I-0970`,
67	after two successive citations in this slot turned out not to support it).
68	Kleiman L5105–L5108: for the conic `u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — smooth, proper,
69	geometrically integral, no rational point, i.e. exactly these binders —
70	`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is **not representable**, while `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is by §4 `th:main`.
71	That is direct. The Zariski route would need "`picSharp` is not a Zariski
72	sheaf", which no source establishes: `ex:Pfs` compares the two *sheafifications*
73	`zar` and `ét` (both already sheaves), and `th:cmp` part 1 gives
74	`picSharp ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` here, so `picSharp` is Zariski-*separated* and any
75	failure could only be gluing. Do **not** rebuild the argument that way.
76	Contrapositive of the quoted fact: representability of `picSharp C` over an
77	arbitrary field is **false in general**, not merely unproved. So the campaign
78	milestones that conclude representability of `picSharp`/`picSharpDeg` over `k`
79	itself — G3 (Galois descent of `picSharp` points) and G4 (the coproduct
80	assembly) — aim at a statement that cannot be proved as written.
81	
82	This is not an argument against the Milne–Kollár route. Everything through J5
83	runs over a separably closed `k'`, where a section is available and the
84	obstruction is absent; the break is precisely at the descent step where the
85	conclusion returns to `k`. The repair the results here name is that the object
86	descended to `k` must be `picEt` and not `picSharp`. Over `k'` the two agree, by
87	`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf` applied to the representability available
88	there — so J5's output is already a `picEt`-representing scheme after base
89	change.
90	
91	**§4 makes the constraint a reduction rather than a quotation**, which is the
92	one place this file goes beyond restating Kleiman.
93	`not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison` proves: if the
94	comparison fails to be an isomorphism then NO scheme represents `picSharp C`.
95	That is Kleiman's own inference at L5105–L5108 ("the two functors differ, so
96	`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable") supplied with a proof, and it is the
97	contrapositive of §3 — no sheaf step, no topology. So a hypothetical proof of
98	G3/G4 as written would prove `picEtComparison` is an isomorphism for *every*
99	curve over *every* field, including pointless ones.
100	
101	What is **not** formalised, and is the whole residue of the argument: that the
102	comparison genuinely fails for that conic. Kleiman's `φ*O(1)` witness runs
103	through `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ` and flat base change. Producing it in Lean is bounded,
104	well-specified work, and §4's theorems are the interface it plugs into. Until
105	then "G3/G4 target a false statement" rests on that one quotation — and on
106	nothing else, which is the improvement.
107	
108	There is one genuine subtlety, and it is not a section. The transport proves
109	that the *same* scheme represents both functors, so it does not produce
110	`picSharp` representability out of nothing — it consumes it. Read
111	`Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` as: the campaign does not
112	need a supplementary étale-representability theorem, only the subcanonicity
113	lemma proved here.
114	
115	## Main results
116	
117	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopology` — the big étale
118	  topology on schemes is subcanonical. Absent from Mathlib `v4.31` as an
119	  instance; obtained from `proetaleTopology` (which has one) along
120	  `Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology` by
121	  `GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le`.
122	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver` — its localisation
123	  to `(Sch/k)`, the site the relative Picard presheaf actually lives on.
124	* `Scheme.PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf` — the section-free
125	  criterion: if `PicSharp.relPresheaf C` is an étale sheaf then
126	  `picEtComparison C` is an isomorphism.
127	* `Scheme.PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy` — representability
128	  of `picSharp C` makes `relPresheaf C` an étale sheaf (subcanonicity, then
129	  reflection along the forgetful functor).
130	* `Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` — the transport: a scheme
131	  representing `picSharp C` also represents `picEt C`, with **no**
132	  `[HasRationalPoint C]`.
133	* `Scheme.hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` — the same statement in
134	  the seam's own packaging: clause (1) of `fgaPicardRepresentability` follows
135	  from its `picSharp` analogue.
136	* `Scheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` — and clause (2)
137	  follows too, *unconditionally*, which is strictly stronger than the seam's
138	  own `HasRationalPoint C → IsIso …`.
139	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy` — §4: a
140	  representable `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf. True and clean, but only half of
141	  the seam's prose argument; see its docstring for why the other half is not
142	  sourced (`I-0970`).
143	* `Scheme.PicScheme.not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison`
144	  and `not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso` — §4's actual payload:
145	  if the comparison is not an isomorphism then NO scheme represents `picSharp C`.
146	  This is Kleiman's non-representability inference (L5105–L5108) as a theorem,
147	  and it needs no sheaf step — only §3.
148	
149	## References
150	
151	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`) — the
152	section route, which this file does not use — and §4 Thm `th:main`.
153	Board: `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`. Decision: `I-0491`.
154	-/

211	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

366	**Expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.**
367	The project reaches this statement rather than proving it, and it is the single
368	named `sorry` that the whole Jacobian headline rests on. Do not replace it with
369	a weaker conditional statement to make a count go down.
370	
371	**Which route discharges it — corrected 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`), because the
372	previous text named the inputs of a route this project does not take.** That
373	text said the inputs are `Div` representability "which needs the Quot scheme"
374	(Kleiman §3 Thm `th:repDiv`) together with the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma
375	`smoothProperQuotient`. Both belong to the **Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient
376	route**, which is `rejected` on the board (`AJC.picrep.quot`,
377	`AJC.picrep.serre`) — so a reader who trusted this docstring concluded, wrongly,
378	that the seam's own inputs had been abandoned.
379	
380	The committed route is **Milne–Kollár** (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`,
381	alternative D3), and it needs neither:
382	
383	* `Div^d` representability comes through the **Grassmannian**, not Quot:
384	  degree slices of `Scheme.DivFunctor` (`Picard/DivDegree.lean`, landed), an
385	  embedding into `Scheme.Grassmannian` of the section module, locally closed
386	  carving, and `Grassmannian.representable`
387	  (`Picard/GrassmannianRepresentability.lean`, proved) — campaign milestones
388	  D1′–D4′. D4′ also delivers the locally closed immersion into `Gr` that serves
389	  as the quasi-projectivity certificate.
390	* the quotient is the **finite Galois** quotient of a semilinear action whose
391	  finite orbits lie in affine opens — campaign G2, in
392	  `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean` (`sorry`-free) with Speiser descent under
393	  `Picard/GaloisDescent/`. It is *not* `smoothProperQuotient`, which is false as
394	  stated in Lean (see the §4 note below) and must not be built against.
395	  **`sorry`-free is not gate-free here**: the affine case is proved
396	  (`isGaloisQuotientSpec`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotientAffine.lean`) and the
397	  gluing substrate exists, but the general existence statement is still the
398	  instance-free class `HasGaloisQuotient` (`FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`), whose
399	  only producer is a single-field non-vacuity witness
400	  (`Picard/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean`). So G2 is *substantially* built, not
401	  discharged.
402	
403	What remains is those campaign modules — uniform `H¹` vanishing (P5, the open
404	`AJC.rr.extuniform` leaf), the `picSharp` Zariski-sheaf/degree/separatedness
405	devices (B1, B4, B6), the `Div^d` chain (D2′–D4′), the Milne glue over a
406	separably closed field (J1–J5, which also needs a universe bridge since
407	`picSharp` is `Type (u+1)`-valued while Mathlib's 01JJ engine wants `Type u`),
408	Galois descent of `picSharp` points (G3), and the coproduct assembly (G4) —
409	**plus one further item that no campaign milestone covers**, recorded next.
410	
411	**THE ELEVENTH ITEM — every campaign milestone targets `picSharp`, while clause
412	(1) above is about `picEt`. CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`ajc-p1`): the gap is a route
413	repair, NOT a missing representability theorem.** The campaign
414	(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`) was written on 2026-07-09 for the
415	`picSharp`-shaped obligation, before the étale decision of 2026-07-28
416	(protection `I-0491`). Its J-cluster represents `picSharpDeg C' r`, G3 descends
417	`picSharp` points, and G4 assembles `picSharpDeg`; the word `picEt` does not
418	occur in any milestone body.
419	
420	The previous text here concluded that the gap "cannot be closed by composing
421	with `picEtComparison`", because that comparison is an isomorphism only under a
422	section (Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5), and hence that representability of the sheafified
423	functor is a *genuine additional obligation*. **That inference was wrong**, and
424	it is a direction confusion. Kleiman 2.5 makes the comparison an isomorphism
425	from a section with no hypothesis on the presheaf; but the comparison is the
426	sheafification *unit*, and a unit is an isomorphism exactly when its source is
427	already a sheaf — and a representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical
428	topology. `Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean` proves this chain
429	(`subcanonical_etaleTopology`, absent from Mathlib `v4.31` for the étale
430	topology but free from `proetaleTopology`), and
431	`picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` transports a `picSharp`
432	representation to a `picEt` one with **no** rational-point hypothesis, the same
433	scheme serving both. So no supplementary étale-representability theorem is
434	needed.
435	
436	**What the correction costs instead, and it is a sharper constraint.**
437	Representability of `picSharp` over an arbitrary field is **FALSE**, so **G3 and
438	G4 target a false statement as written**, not a hard one. The source says so
439	directly: Kleiman L5105–L5108 on the conic `u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — smooth,
440	proper, geometrically integral, no rational point — `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not
441	representable while `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is.
442	
443	**This does not go through the Zariski-sheaf theorem, and an earlier revision of
444	this paragraph wrongly said it did** (`I-0970`). The Lean statement
445	`PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy` is true and useful, but
446	its contrapositive needs "`picSharp` is not a Zariski sheaf", which no source
447	here establishes — `ex:Pfs` compares the two *sheafifications*, and `th:cmp`
448	part 1 shows `picSharp ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` on these binders, so it is
449	Zariski-*separated*. The route that does work is
450	`not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso` (see the sheafification paragraph
451	above): comparison-failure alone refutes representability, with no topology in
452	the argument. Everything through J5 runs over a separably closed
453	`k'` where a section is available and the obstruction absent; the break is the
454	descent step where the conclusion returns to `k`, and the repair is that the
455	object descended must be `picEt` (which has the sheaf property that carries
456	descent) rather than `picSharp`. Over `k'` the two agree. Restating G3/G4 that
457	way reaches clause (1) with no false intermediate.
458	
459	Not formalised, and named as such: that Kleiman's non-sheaf curve satisfies this
460	file's binders (smooth, proper, geometrically integral) is quoted from the
461	reference rather than proved. Tracked as `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`; the board node
462	`AJC.picrep` carries the landed/absent split.
463	
464	**The repair has a third input, and until 2026-07-29 no site named it**
465	(`review-ajc`, `AJC.picrep.etale-rep.crossbase`). "Descend `picEt` instead of
466	`picSharp`" needs three things, not two. Two exist: `Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean`
467	proves `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k` is an étale cover and that `picEt` satisfies its sheaf
468	axiom at every test (the descent *test*), and `G1`/`G2` supply the Galois action
469	and the quotient. The third is the **cross-base identification**: for a `k'`-test
470	`T`,
471	
472	  `picEt C` at `(Over.map (Spec.map (algebraMap k k'))).obj T`
473	    ≅ `picEt (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')` at `T`.
474	
475	Without it the scheme `J5` produces over `k'` represents `picEt` *of the curve
476	over `k`, restricted to `k'`-tests* rather than `picEt` of the base-changed
477	curve, and there is no functor for the descent datum to be a datum *for*.
478	Measured: the statement type-checks in this project (the base-changed curve
479	inherits both binders, `RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean:256`), and it is absent.
480	
481	The absence rests on a **token scan, not on an enumeration being complete** — and
482	that distinction is the point. Every `picEt`-mentioning declaration in this project
483	was scanned for `baseChange`, `algebraMap` and `Over.map`; the only occurrence of
484	the cross-base shape anywhere in `AlgebraicJacobian/` is the prose above. Two
485	earlier revisions of this paragraph instead offered a list called "the complete
486	list", and **both lists were wrong**: the first named
487	`picEt_isSheaf_etaleTopologyOver`, which `ajc-p1` deleted hours later as a
488	duplicate of `picEt_isSheaf_forget` (`I-1075`), and the second omitted six
489	declarations, including `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` and
490	`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf` in `PicEtSubcanonical.lean` (found by a
491	fresh-context audit of this very correction). Neither error touched the
492	conclusion, because none of the missed or deleted declarations relates the functor
493	of `C` to the functor of a base change of `C` — which is exactly why the scan, and
494	not the census, is what the claim should have rested on from the start.
495

100	open CategoryTheory Limits
101	
102	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
103	
104	namespace Scheme
105	
106	namespace Modules
107	
108	/-- **Restriction of `⊗` to the `LineBundle.OnProduct` carrier.**
109	
110	For `S`-schemes `C, T`, the bifunctor `⊗_{C ×_S T}` restricts to the subtype
111	`LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT` of locally-trivial modules on `C ×_S T`, with unit
112	the structure sheaf and the dual as two-sided inverse. Per blueprint
113	`lem:tensorobj_lift_onproduct`: the carrier is `tensorObj L.carrier L'.carrier`, and
114	local triviality is `tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial`. -/
115	noncomputable def tensorObjOnProduct {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S)
116	    (L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT :=
117	  ⟨tensorObj L.carrier L'.carrier,
118	    tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial L.isLocallyTrivial L'.isLocallyTrivial⟩
119	
120	end Modules
121	
122	namespace PicSharp
123	
124	/-! ## §1. Abelian-group structure on the relative Picard quotient
125	
126	The Picard group `Pic(X)` of any scheme is canonically an abelian group
127	under tensor product of line bundles (Stacks tag 01CR; the inverse of
128	`[L]` is `[L⁻¹] = [Hom_{O_X}(L, O_X)]`). The pullback map
129	`π_T^* : Pic(T) → Pic(C ×_k T)` of
130	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection`
131	respects this structure: it sends `O_T ↦ O_{C ×_k T}` (the structure
132	sheaf is preserved by inverse image) and is multiplicative on tensor
133	products (Stacks 01HH for invertibility, Mathlib's
134	`Scheme.Modules.pullback` for the underlying multiplicativity).
135	
136	Therefore `π_T^* Pic(T)` is a subgroup of `Pic(C ×_k T)`, and the
137	quotient `Pic(C ×_k T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` inherits a canonical
138	abelian-group structure under which the quotient map is a surjective
139	homomorphism with kernel exactly `π_T^* Pic(T)`.
140	
141	Blueprint reference: `lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid` (Kleiman §2,
142	Defs. `df:aPf` + `df:Pfs`; Stacks tag 01CR). -/
143	
144	/-! ### Substrate for the relative-Picard group law
145	
146	The carrier setoid `RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup` is the **iso-class** equivalence
147	`Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)` on the locally-trivial line bundles on `C ×_S T`,
148	*not* the quotient-by-`H_T` relation. Hence `Quotient (preimage_subgroup πC πT)` is
149	`Pic(C ×_S T)` itself, and the `AddCommGroup` on it is the **tensor-product Picard
150	group** — the additive mirror of the absolute `picCommGroup`. The blueprint's Steps 2–4
151	(`pullbackHom`, `H_T := pullbackHom.range`, setoid reconciliation, transport) describe
152	the *other* carrier, the `H_T`-quotient built in §1b below; they do not apply to the
153	iso-class carrier.
154	
155	The group law is built from the upstream substrate of `Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean`
156	(`Modules.tensorObj`, `Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso`, the unitors, the braiding,
157	`Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso`, `Modules.tensorObjOnProduct`,
158	`Modules.tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial`), not from a monoidal-category instance on
159	`Scheme.Modules`: `zero` is `isLocallyTrivial_unit`, and `neg`/`neg_add_cancel` use
160	`Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`, the reverse bridge
161	`IsLocallyTrivial ⟹ IsInvertible`. -/
162	
163	/-- The structure sheaf is locally trivial (it restricts to the structure sheaf on
164	every affine open). On any affine chart `W ∋ x`: the restriction of the unit is
165	its pullback (`restrictFunctorIsoPullback`), and the pullback of the unit is the
166	unit (`pullbackUnitIso`); compose to trivialise `(𝒪_X)|_W ≅ 𝒪_W`. -/
167	private theorem isLocallyTrivial_unit {X : Scheme.{u}} :
168	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) := by
169	  intro x
170	  obtain ⟨W, hW_aff, hxW, _⟩ :=
171	    exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (X := X) (x := x) (U := ⊤)
172	      (show x ∈ (⊤ : X.Opens) from trivial)
173	  refine ⟨W, hxW, hW_aff, ?_⟩
174	  exact ⟨(Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback W.ι).app _ ≪≫ Modules.pullbackUnitIso W.ι⟩
175	
176	/-- Uniqueness of the tensor inverse up to iso (mirror of `IsInvertible.inverse_unique`). -/
177	private theorem pInverseUnique {X : Scheme.{u}} {M N N' : X.Modules}
178	    (e : Modules.tensorObj M N ≅ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)
179	    (e' : Modules.tensorObj M N' ≅ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) :
180	    Nonempty (N ≅ N') :=
181	  ⟨(Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor N).symm ≪≫
182	    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl N) e'.symm ≪≫
183	    (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso (M := N) (N := M) (P := N')).symm ≪≫
184	    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.tensorObj_braiding N M ≪≫ e) (Iso.refl N') ≪≫
185	    Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor N'⟩
186	
187	/-- The addition carrier: `[L] + [L'] := [L ⊗ L']`, lifted to the loc-triv carrier
188	`OnProduct`; this is `Modules.tensorObjOnProduct`. -/
189	private noncomputable def relTensorObj {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
190	    (L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT :=
191	  Modules.tensorObjOnProduct πC πT L L'
192	
193	/-- Descended addition on the relative Picard quotient: well-defined on iso-classes
194	by bifunctoriality (`Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso`). Mirror of `picMul`. -/
195	private noncomputable def relAdd {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S} :
196	    Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT) →
197	      Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT) →
198	      Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT) :=
199	  Quotient.lift₂
200	    (fun L L' => Quotient.mk _ (relTensorObj L L'))
201	    (by
202	      rintro L L' M M' ⟨e⟩ ⟨e'⟩
203	      exact Quotient.sound ⟨Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso e e'⟩)
204	
205	/-- Descended negation on the relative Picard quotient: `-[L] := [Linv]` for the
206	inverse witness of `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`, well-defined by
207	`pInverseUnique`. Mirror of `picInv`. -/
208	private noncomputable def relNeg {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S} :
209	    Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT) →
210	      Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT) :=
211	  Quotient.lift
212	    (fun L => Quotient.mk _
213	      (⟨Classical.choose (Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse L.isLocallyTrivial),
214	        (Classical.choose_spec (Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse L.isLocallyTrivial)).1⟩ :
215	        LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT))
216	    (by
217	      rintro L M ⟨e⟩
218	      refine Quotient.sound ?_
219	      have h1 :=
220	        (Classical.choose_spec (Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse L.isLocallyTrivial)).2.some
221	      have h2 := Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso e (Iso.refl _) ≪≫
222	        (Classical.choose_spec (Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse M.isLocallyTrivial)).2.some
223	      exact pInverseUnique h1 h2)
224	
225	/-- **Abelian-group instance on the ABSOLUTE Picard group** `Pic(C ×_S T)`.
226	
227	For a base scheme `S`, a curve-side morphism `πC : C ⟶ S`, and a test
228	object `πT : T ⟶ S`, the quotient set
229	```
230	Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT)  =  Pic(C ×_S T)
231	```
232	is the set of **iso-classes** of locally-trivial line bundles on
233	`C ×_S T` — the carrier setoid `RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup` is the
234	iso-class relation `Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)`, NOT the coset
235	relation by `π_T^* Pic(T)`. So this is the absolute Picard group, the
236	additive mirror of `picCommGroup`; the RELATIVE quotient
237	`Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` that `lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid` names is
238	`PicSharp.addCommGroup_via_tensorObj` on `Quotient (relPicSetoid πC πT)`
239	below.
240	
241	It carries a canonical abelian-group structure: addition is the descent of
242	tensor product `[L] + [L'] := [L ⊗ L']`, the zero element is the class
243	`[O_{C ×_S T}]`, and the inverse is `-[L] := [L⁻¹]` (the dual line
244	bundle). The absolute group is consumed by the relative construction below.
245	
246	The carrier `LineBundle.OnProduct` is `{ M : (pullback πC πT).Modules // IsLocallyTrivial M }`
247	(`LineBundlePullback.lean`), and the tensor-product group law is built directly from the
248	substrate of `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean` (`Modules.tensorObj`,
249	`Modules.tensorObjOnProduct`, the coherence isos

300	/-! ## §1b. The relative Picard `H_T`-coset setoid
301	
302	`PicSharp.addCommGroup` lives on `Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT)`,
303	whose carrier setoid is the **iso-class** relation `Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)` — i.e. the
304	**absolute** `Pic(C ×_S T)`. The blueprint (`lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, Kleiman §2 `df:Pfs`) asks
305	instead for the **relative** quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`, the quotient by the subgroup
306	`H_T := im π_T^*`. This section builds that quotient directly as a coarser setoid
307	`relPicSetoid` on `LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT`, together with the abelian-group instance
308	`PicSharp.addCommGroup_via_tensorObj` on it.
309	
310	**Relation (multiplicative form).** For `L L' : OnProduct πC πT` set
311	```
312	L ~ L'   ↔   ∃ N locally trivial on T,  L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier,
313	```
314	where `π_T^* N = (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier`. This is the left-coset
315	relation of `H_T := im π_T^*`. It is **equivalent** to the blueprint's `L ⊗ L'^{-1} ≅ π_T^* N`
316	(tensor both sides by `L'` / its inverse), but the multiplicative form avoids naming the tensor
317	inverse of `L'` in the *definition* — only the setoid-symmetry step consumes a tensor inverse (of
318	`N` on the base `T`, via `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`). The blueprint statements
319	`lem:relpic_setoid_{refl,symm,trans}`, `lem:relpic_add_welldef` and `lem:pullback_inverse_iso`

9	/-!
10	# Subcanonicity of the étale site, and the section-free transport `picSharp → picEt`
11	
12	This file settles a **route** question about the project's central obligation
13	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), and
14	it settles it in the direction opposite to what that file's docstring and the
15	board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep` currently assert.
16	
17	## The claim this file refutes
18	
19	Clause (1) of the seam asks for representability of the étale-sheafified
20	functor `PicScheme.picEt C`, while every milestone of the Milne–Kollár campaign
21	targets the *unsheafified* `PicScheme.picSharp C`. The seam docstring and the
22	board row both say the gap between them **cannot be bridged without a
23	`k`-rational point**, on the grounds that the comparison
24	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 — an isomorphism only under
25	a section — and that a section is exactly what the owner decision `I-0491`
26	forbids the headline to carry.
27	
28	That reasoning is wrong, and the error is a direction confusion. Kleiman §2
29	Thm 2.5 is the statement that a section makes the comparison an isomorphism
30	*with no hypothesis on the presheaf*. But there is a second, entirely
31	independent, route to the same conclusion: the comparison is the sheafification
32	unit, and a unit is an isomorphism **exactly when its source is already a
33	sheaf** (`CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify`). A representable functor is a sheaf
34	for any subcanonical topology. So *if* the campaign delivers representability of
35	`picSharp`, the source is a sheaf for that reason alone, the unit is an
36	isomorphism, and no section is involved anywhere.
37	
38	The consequence for the route, stated precisely because the board row is
39	currently priced on its negation: the campaign's endpoint **is** transportable
40	to clause (1). `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` below is that
41	transport, proved with no rational-point hypothesis of any kind.
42	
43	## What is actually still open
44	
45	This file does **not** close the seam. It removes an alleged obstruction, which
46	is a different thing, and the honest statement of what remains is:
47	
48	* the antecedent of every theorem here is representability of `picSharp C`
49	  over an arbitrary field — campaign milestones J1–J5, G3, G4, B1/B4/B6,
50	  D2′–D4′, P5 — and **not one of those is discharged**. No theorem in this file
51	  is applied to a curve anywhere in the project, and none should be reported as
52	  progress on the existence question;
53	* what changes is the *shape* of the remaining work. Before this file, a reader
54	  of the seam docstring concluded that finishing the campaign leaves a further
55	  unpriced obligation ("represent `picEt` directly, or restate the headline").
56	  After it, no supplementary étale-representability theorem is needed: `picEt`
57	  representability follows from `picSharp` representability by `Subcanonical` +
58	  `isIso_toSheafify`, both already in Mathlib.
59	
60	**But the antecedent must not be read as reachable over `k`, and §4 is why.**
61	The same subcanonicity that powers the transport also proves that a
62	representable `picSharp` is a *Zariski* sheaf
63	(`PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`).
64	
65	**But the falsity of `picSharp` representability is quoted from Kleiman, NOT
66	derived from that theorem** — corrected 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc` / `I-0970`,
67	after two successive citations in this slot turned out not to support it).
68	Kleiman L5105–L5108: for the conic `u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — smooth, proper,
69	geometrically integral, no rational point, i.e. exactly these binders —
70	`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is **not representable**, while `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is by §4 `th:main`.
71	That is direct. The Zariski route would need "`picSharp` is not a Zariski
72	sheaf", which no source establishes: `ex:Pfs` compares the two *sheafifications*
73	`zar` and `ét` (both already sheaves), and `th:cmp` part 1 gives
74	`picSharp ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` here, so `picSharp` is Zariski-*separated* and any
75	failure could only be gluing. Do **not** rebuild the argument that way.
76	Contrapositive of the quoted fact: representability of `picSharp C` over an
77	arbitrary field is **false in general**, not merely unproved. So the campaign
78	milestones that conclude representability of `picSharp`/`picSharpDeg` over `k`
79	itself — G3 (Galois descent of `picSharp` points) and G4 (the coproduct
80	assembly) — aim at a statement that cannot be proved as written.
81	
82	This is not an argument against the Milne–Kollár route. Everything through J5
83	runs over a separably closed `k'`, where a section is available and the
84	obstruction is absent; the break is precisely at the descent step where the
85	conclusion returns to `k`. The repair the results here name is that the object
86	descended to `k` must be `picEt` and not `picSharp`. Over `k'` the two agree, by
87	`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf` applied to the representability available
88	there — so J5's output is already a `picEt`-representing scheme after base
89	change.
90	
91	**§4 makes the constraint a reduction rather than a quotation**, which is the
92	one place this file goes beyond restating Kleiman.
93	`not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison` proves: if the
94	comparison fails to be an isomorphism then NO scheme represents `picSharp C`.
95	That is Kleiman's own inference at L5105–L5108 ("the two functors differ, so
96	`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable") supplied with a proof, and it is the
97	contrapositive of §3 — no sheaf step, no topology. So a hypothetical proof of
98	G3/G4 as written would prove `picEtComparison` is an isomorphism for *every*
99	curve over *every* field, including pointless ones.
100	
101	What is **not** formalised, and is the whole residue of the argument: that the
102	comparison genuinely fails for that conic. Kleiman's `φ*O(1)` witness runs
103	through `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ` and flat base change. Producing it in Lean is bounded,
104	well-specified work, and §4's theorems are the interface it plugs into. Until
105	then "G3/G4 target a false statement" rests on that one quotation — and on
106	nothing else, which is the improvement.
107	
108	There is one genuine subtlety, and it is not a section. The transport proves
109	that the *same* scheme represents both functors, so it does not produce
110	`picSharp` representability out of nothing — it consumes it. Read
111	`Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` as: the campaign does not
112	need a supplementary étale-representability theorem, only the subcanonicity
113	lemma proved here.
114	
115	## Main results
116	
117	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopology` — the big étale
118	  topology on schemes is subcanonical. Absent from Mathlib `v4.31` as an
119	  instance; obtained from `proetaleTopology` (which has one) along
120	  `Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology` by
121	  `GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le`.
122	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver` — its localisation
123	  to `(Sch/k)`, the site the relative Picard presheaf actually lives on.
124	* `Scheme.PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf` — the section-free
125	  criterion: if `PicSharp.relPresheaf C` is an étale sheaf then
126	  `picEtComparison C` is an isomorphism.
127	* `Scheme.PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy` — representability
128	  of `picSharp C` makes `relPresheaf C` an étale sheaf (subcanonicity, then
129	  reflection along the forgetful functor).
130	* `Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` — the transport: a scheme
131	  representing `picSharp C` also represents `picEt C`, with **no**
132	  `[HasRationalPoint C]`.
133	* `Scheme.hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` — the same statement in
134	  the seam's own packaging: clause (1) of `fgaPicardRepresentability` follows
135	  from its `picSharp` analogue.
136	* `Scheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` — and clause (2)
137	  follows too, *unconditionally*, which is strictly stronger than the seam's
138	  own `HasRationalPoint C → IsIso …`.
139	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy` — §4: a
140	  representable `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf. True and clean, but only half of
141	  the seam's prose argument; see its docstring for why the other half is not
142	  sourced (`I-0970`).
143	* `Scheme.PicScheme.not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison`
144	  and `not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso` — §4's actual payload:
145	  if the comparison is not an isomorphism then NO scheme represents `picSharp C`.
146	  This is Kleiman's non-representability inference (L5105–L5108) as a theorem,
147	  and it needs no sheaf step — only §3.
148

166	/-! ## §1. The étale site is subcanonical -/
167	
168	/-- **The big étale topology on schemes is subcanonical**, i.e. every
169	representable presheaf is an étale sheaf.
170	
171	Mathlib `v4.31` supplies this instance for the Zariski, coherent, regular,
172	extensive and *pro*-étale topologies, but not for the étale one. It costs
173	nothing: `Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology` and
174	`GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le` (a subtopology of a subcanonical
175	topology is subcanonical, since the canonical topology is an upper bound).
176	
177	This is the lemma that makes the transport of §3 possible, and its absence is
178	why the seam's route analysis concluded a section was needed. -/
179	instance subcanonical_etaleTopology : Scheme.etaleTopology.{u}.Subcanonical :=
180	  GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology
181	
182	/-- Subcanonicity descends to the localisation `(Sch/k)`, which is the site the
183	relative Picard presheaf lives on (`Scheme.etaleTopologyOver`,
184	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`).
185	
186	Supplied by `GrothendieckTopology.subcanonical_over` from
187	`subcanonical_etaleTopology`; recorded as a named theorem because the
188	`etaleTopologyOver` abbreviation is what every statement downstream mentions. -/
189	theorem subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
190	    (etaleTopologyOver k).Subcanonical :=
191	  inferInstance

195	/-! ## §2. The comparison is an isomorphism when the source is a sheaf -/
196	
197	/-- **The section-free criterion for the sheafification comparison.**
198	
199	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is by construction the sheafification unit
200	`PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C` whiskered with the forgetful functor. A unit of the
201	sheafification adjunction is an isomorphism exactly when its source is already
202	a sheaf (`CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify`), so the étale sheaf property of
203	`PicSharp.relPresheaf C` suffices — and nothing about `C(k)` enters.
204	
205	Contrast `picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`
206	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), which reaches the same conclusion from
207	Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 via a section. The two routes are independent; this one is
208	the one available under the owner decision `I-0491`. -/
209	theorem isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k]
210	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
211	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
212	    (h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)) :
213	    IsIso (picEtComparison C) :=
214	  haveI : IsIso (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C) := isIso_toSheafify _ h
215	  Functor.isIso_whiskerRight _ _
216	
217	/-- **Representability makes the relative Picard presheaf an étale sheaf.**
218	
219	Two steps, both structural. A functor represented by a scheme is a sheaf for
220	the subcanonical étale topology
221	(`GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable`, using
222	`subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver`); and the sheaf property of the
223	`AddCommGrpCat`-valued `relPresheaf C` is *equivalent* to that of its
224	underlying type-valued functor `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _`, because
225	the forgetful functor of a concrete algebraic category preserves limits and
226	reflects isomorphisms (`Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget`).
227	
228	The hypothesis is a `RepresentableBy` for an arbitrary `X`, not for
229	`PicScheme C`, so this does not silently consume the seam. -/
230	theorem relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy {k : Type u} [Field k]
231	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
232	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
233	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
234	    (rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
235	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) := by
236	  haveI : (picSharp C).IsRepresentable := ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩⟩
237	  have hsh : Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picSharp C) :=
238	    GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable _
239	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget (s := CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}),
240	    CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type]
241	  exact hsh
242	
243	end PicScheme

245	/-! ## §3. The transport, with no rational point anywhere -/
246	
247	/-- **The transport: a scheme representing `picSharp C` also represents
248	`picEt C`, with no hypothesis on `C(k)`.**
249	
250	This is the statement the seam docstring and the board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`
251	declare impossible without a section. The proof composes §1 and §2: the
252	representing scheme makes `relPresheaf C` an étale sheaf
253	(`relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`, i.e. subcanonicity), being a sheaf
254	makes the sheafification unit an isomorphism
255	(`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf`), and `Functor.RepresentableBy.ofIso`
256	carries the representation across it.

258	Note what is and is not proved. `X` is *given* here — the theorem consumes
259	`picSharp` representability rather than producing it, and that antecedent is
260	exactly the undischarged output of the Milne–Kollár campaign. What the theorem
261	establishes is that no *further* representability theorem is needed on top of
262	the campaign, contradicting the "eleventh item" pricing. -/
263	noncomputable def picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport {k : Type u} [Field k]
264	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
265	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
266	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
267	    (rep : (PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
268	    (PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X :=
269	  rep.ofIso (@asIso _ _ _ _ (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)
270	    (PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf C
271	      (PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy C rep)))

273	/-- **Clause (1) of the seam follows from its `picSharp` analogue.**
274	
275	Same content as `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport`, packaged in the
276	seam's own existential shape so the comparison with
277	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is direct: the local-finiteness and
278	separatedness conjuncts are carried across unchanged, because the transport
279	does not move the representing scheme — it is the *same* `X`.

282	`[HasPicScheme C]`, deliberately: `HasPicScheme` pins the witness to
283	`PicScheme C` and has no instance, so quantifying over it would make this
284	theorem consume an uninhabited class. Here the witness is universally
285	quantified and the statement is a genuine implication. -/
286	theorem hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability {k : Type u} [Field k]
287	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
288	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
289	    (h : ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
290	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
291	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom) :
292	    ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
293	      Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
294	        LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom := by
295	  obtain ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, hft, hsep⟩ := h
296	  exact ⟨X, ⟨picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport C rep⟩, hft, hsep⟩

299	than the seam's own second conjunct `HasRationalPoint C → IsIso …`.

302	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is an isomorphism outright, with no section. So

310	theorem isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability {k : Type u} [Field k]
311	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
312	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
313	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
314	    (rep : (PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
315	    IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C) :=

409	argument runs through `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ` and flat base change. That is a bounded,
410	well-specified piece of work, and this theorem is the interface it would plug
411	into. -/
412	theorem not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
413	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
11	
12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
16	
17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
18	
19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
21	a sheaf** (Kleiman §2, L1330: "not *a priori* a sheaf"), and over a general
22	field it is **not representable** — the witness is Exercise `ex:Pfs`, the conic
23	`u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, smooth proper geometrically integral with no rational
24	point.
25	
26	**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`).** This paragraph asserted
27	non-sheafness "not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302)",
28	and glossed it as: a line bundle can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T`
29	without being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`. Both the citation and the gloss are
30	wrong. L1292–L1302 proves that the **absolute** functor `Pic_X` is never a
31	separated Zariski presheaf, using `T = ℙ¹_X`; the quotient by `π_T^* Pic(T)`
32	that defines the *relative* functor is exactly what kills that argument, and
33	L1600–L1605 in fact proves `Pic_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` when `f` has a section.
34	Sheafifying is still the right move and the conclusion below is unaffected —
35	only the stated reason was. Full account in
36	`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`'s module docstring.
37	
38	Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
39	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
40	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
41	hypothesis.
42	
43	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
44	supplied:
45	
46	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
47	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
48	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
49	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
50	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
51	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
52	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
53	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
54	
55	## The site
56	
57	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
58	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
59	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
60	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
61	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
62	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
63	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
64	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
65	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
66	hypothesis.
67	
68	## Main definitions
69	
70	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
71	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
72	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
73	  relative Picard presheaf.
74	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
75	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
76	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
77	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
78	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
79	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
80	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
81	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
82	  must match.
83	
84	## References
85	
86	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
87	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
88	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
89	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
90	-/

140	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
141	
142	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
143	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
144	
145	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
146	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
147	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
148	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
149	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
150	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally.
151	
152	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
153	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
154	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
155	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
156	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
157	the relative functor that is sheafified here.
158	
159	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
160	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
161	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful

124	/-! ## §1. Abelian-group structure on the relative Picard quotient
125	
126	The Picard group `Pic(X)` of any scheme is canonically an abelian group
127	under tensor product of line bundles (Stacks tag 01CR; the inverse of
128	`[L]` is `[L⁻¹] = [Hom_{O_X}(L, O_X)]`). The pullback map
129	`π_T^* : Pic(T) → Pic(C ×_k T)` of
130	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection`
131	respects this structure: it sends `O_T ↦ O_{C ×_k T}` (the structure
132	sheaf is preserved by inverse image) and is multiplicative on tensor
133	products (Stacks 01HH for invertibility, Mathlib's
134	`Scheme.Modules.pullback` for the underlying multiplicativity).
135	
136	Therefore `π_T^* Pic(T)` is a subgroup of `Pic(C ×_k T)`, and the
137	quotient `Pic(C ×_k T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` inherits a canonical
138	abelian-group structure under which the quotient map is a surjective
139	homomorphism with kernel exactly `π_T^* Pic(T)`.

142	Defs. `df:aPf` + `df:Pfs`; Stacks tag 01CR). -/

301	
302	`PicSharp.addCommGroup` lives on `Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT)`,
303	whose carrier setoid is the **iso-class** relation `Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)` — i.e. the
304	**absolute** `Pic(C ×_S T)`. The blueprint (`lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, Kleiman §2 `df:Pfs`) asks
305	instead for the **relative** quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`, the quotient by the subgroup
306	`H_T := im π_T^*`. This section builds that quotient directly as a coarser setoid
307	`relPicSetoid` on `LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT`, together with the abelian-group instance

310	**Relation (multiplicative form).** For `L L' : OnProduct πC πT` set
311	```
312	L ~ L'   ↔   ∃ N locally trivial on T,  L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier,
313	```
314	where `π_T^* N = (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier`. This is the left-coset
315	relation of `H_T := im π_T^*`. It is **equivalent** to the blueprint's `L ⊗ L'^{-1} ≅ π_T^* N`

335	theorem relPicRel_of_iso {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}

377	theorem relPicRel_trans {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}

379	    (h : relPicRel πC πT L L') (h' : relPicRel πC πT L' L'') :

396	def relPicSetoid {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) :

403	private noncomputable def tensorMiddleFour {X : Scheme.{u}} (A B C D : X.Modules) :

10	/-!
11	# Rigidified relative Picard bundles (B1: the `RigidifiedPic` API)
12	
13	For a relative curve `πC : C ⟶ S` with a **section of the projection**
14	`σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` (i.e. `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`, where `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`), Kleiman's
15	rigidification of the relative Picard functor replaces a bare line bundle `L` on
16	`C ×_S T` by a *rigidified* one — a bundle equipped with a trivialisation of its
17	restriction `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T` along the section. Rigidified bundles have no non-trivial
18	automorphisms (`lm:aut`, the ring-level heart of which is
19	`StructureSheafPushforward.eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one_of_gate`), so the
20	rigidified functor is a Zariski sheaf and represents the relative Picard functor.
21	
22	This file supplies the substrate of that programme:
23	
24	* `sectionPullbackProjIso` — the section base-change iso `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N` (from
25	  `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T` via the pullback pseudofunctor);
26	* `Rigidification σ L` — a trivialisation `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`;
27	* `exists_rigidification_relPicRel` — **Kleiman `lm:fff`**: every `L` is
28	  `H_T`-equivalent to a rigidified bundle `L' = L ⊗ π_T^*((σ^* L)⁻¹)`;
29	* `rationalPointSection` — the section `σ_T` of the projection produced by a
30	  `k`-rational point `x₀` of `C`, matching the hypothesis shape consumed by the
31	  `StructureSheafPushforward` `lm:aut` lemmas.
32	
33	Blueprint references: Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, Lemmas `lm:fff` (existence of the
34	rigidified representative), `lm:aut` (automorphism-freeness). The `H_T`-relation
35	`PicSharp.relPicRel` is the one of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean`.
36	-/
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Limits

42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	namespace Scheme

46	namespace PicSharp

48	/-! ## §1. The section base-change isomorphism -/
49	
50	/-- **Section base-change iso** `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N`.
51	
52	For a section `σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` of the projection `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`
53	(so `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`) and a sheaf of modules `N` on `T`, the pullback pseudofunctor
54	identity `(σ ≫ π_T)^* ≅ σ^* ∘ π_T^*` together with `𝟙_T^* ≅ id` identifies the
55	double pullback `σ^*(π_T^* N)` with `N`. This is the same three-step
56	`pullbackComp`/`pullbackCongr`/`pullbackId` chain as `LineBundle.pullback_pullback_eq`,
57	specialised to a section. -/
58	noncomputable def sectionPullbackProjIso {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
59	    (σ : T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT)
60	    (hσ : σ ≫ Limits.pullback.snd πC πT = 𝟙 T) (N : T.Modules) :
61	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj
62	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).obj N) ≅ N :=
63	  (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp σ (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).app N ≪≫
64	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr hσ).app N ≪≫ (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId T).app N
65	
66	/-! ## §2. Rigidifications -/
67	
68	/-- A **rigidification** of a line bundle `L` on `C ×_S T` along a section `σ` of the
69	projection is a trivialisation of the restriction `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`. -/
70	structure Rigidification {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
71	    (σ : T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT) (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) where
72	  /-- The trivialising isomorphism `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`. -/
73	  triv : (Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj L.carrier ≅ SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf
74	
75	/-! ## §3. Existence of a rigidified representative (`lm:fff`) -/
76	
77	/-- **Existence of a rigidified representative** (Kleiman §2, `lm:fff`).
78	
79	Every line bundle `L` on `C ×_S T` is `H_T`-equivalent (`PicSharp.relPicRel`) to a
80	line bundle `L'` carrying a rigidification along the section `σ`. Explicitly
81	`L' = L ⊗ π_T^*((σ^* L)⁻¹)`: its restriction along `σ` is
82	`σ^*L ⊗ σ^*(π_T^*(σ^*L)⁻¹) ≅ σ^*L ⊗ (σ^*L)⁻¹ ≅ 𝒪_T`
83	(using the section base-change iso `sectionPullbackProjIso`), and `L' ≅ π_T^*((σ^*L)⁻¹) ⊗ L`
84	differs from `L` by a pullback from the base, hence `[L'] = [L]` in
85	`Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`. -/
86	theorem exists_rigidification_relPicRel {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
87	    (σ : T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT)

module

public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.Descent.DescentData

/-!
# Stacks: effectiveness of descent

Let `C` be a category with a Grothendieck topology `J` and `F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat`.
In this file, we define the typeclass `F.IsStack J` saying that `F` is a stack for `J`.
(See the terminological note in the file `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Descent/IsPrestack.lean`:
we do not require that the categories `F.obj (.mk (op S))` are groupoids.)

The typeclass `IsStack` extends `IsPrestack`. The effectiveness of descent that
is required for stacks is expressed by saying that the functors `toDescentData`
attached to covering sieves are essentially surjective. Together with the
`IsPrestack` assumption, we get that these functors are actually equivalences of
categories (see `isEquivalence_toDescentData`). Conversely, we provide a
constructor `IsStack.of_isStackFor` which assumes that these functors are
equivalences of categories.

## References
* [Jean Giraud, *Cohomologie non abélienne*][giraud1971]
* [Gérard Laumon and Laurent Moret-Bailly, *Champs algébriques*][laumon-morel-bailly-2000]

-/

10	/-!
11	# Rigidified relative Picard bundles (B1: the `RigidifiedPic` API)
12	
13	For a relative curve `πC : C ⟶ S` with a **section of the projection**
14	`σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` (i.e. `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`, where `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`), Kleiman's
15	rigidification of the relative Picard functor replaces a bare line bundle `L` on
16	`C ×_S T` by a *rigidified* one — a bundle equipped with a trivialisation of its
17	restriction `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T` along the section. Rigidified bundles have no non-trivial
18	automorphisms (`lm:aut`, the ring-level heart of which is
19	`StructureSheafPushforward.eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one_of_gate`), so the
20	rigidified functor is a Zariski sheaf and represents the relative Picard functor.
21	
22	This file supplies the substrate of that programme:
23	
24	* `sectionPullbackProjIso` — the section base-change iso `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N` (from
25	  `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T` via the pullback pseudofunctor);
26	* `Rigidification σ L` — a trivialisation `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`;
27	* `exists_rigidification_relPicRel` — **Kleiman `lm:fff`**: every `L` is
28	  `H_T`-equivalent to a rigidified bundle `L' = L ⊗ π_T^*((σ^* L)⁻¹)`;
29	* `rationalPointSection` — the section `σ_T` of the projection produced by a
30	  `k`-rational point `x₀` of `C`, matching the hypothesis shape consumed by the
31	  `StructureSheafPushforward` `lm:aut` lemmas.
32	
33	Blueprint references: Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, Lemmas `lm:fff` (existence of the
34	rigidified representative), `lm:aut` (automorphism-freeness). The `H_T`-relation
35	`PicSharp.relPicRel` is the one of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean`.
36	-/
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Limits
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	namespace Scheme
45	
46	namespace PicSharp
47	
48	/-! ## §1. The section base-change isomorphism -/
49	
50	/-- **Section base-change iso** `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N`.
51	
52	For a section `σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` of the projection `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`
53	(so `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`) and a sheaf of modules `N` on `T`, the pullback pseudofunctor
54	identity `(σ ≫ π_T)^* ≅ σ^* ∘ π_T^*` together with `𝟙_T^* ≅ id` identifies the
55	double pullback `σ^*(π_T^* N)` with `N`. This is the same three-step
56	`pullbackComp`/`pullbackCongr`/`pullbackId` chain as `LineBundle.pullback_pullback_eq`,
57	specialised to a section. -/
58	noncomputable def sectionPullbackProjIso {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
59	    (σ : T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT)
60	    (hσ : σ ≫ Limits.pullback.snd πC πT = 𝟙 T) (N : T.Modules) :
61	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj
62	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).obj N) ≅ N :=
63	  (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp σ (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).app N ≪≫
64	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr hσ).app N ≪≫ (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId T).app N
65	
66	/-! ## §2. Rigidifications -/
67	
68	/-- A **rigidification** of a line bundle `L` on `C ×_S T` along a section `σ` of the
69	projection is a trivialisation of the restriction `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`. -/
70	structure Rigidification {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
71	    (σ : T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT) (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) where
72	  /-- The trivialising isomorphism `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`. -/
73	  triv : (Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj L.carrier ≅ SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf
74	
75	/-! ## §3. Existence of a rigidified representative (`lm:fff`) -/
76	
77	/-- **Existence of a rigidified representative** (Kleiman §2, `lm:fff`).
78	
79	Every line bundle `L` on `C ×_S T` is `H_T`-equivalent (`PicSharp.relPicRel`) to a
80	line bundle `L'` carrying a rigidification along the section `σ`. Explicitly
81	`L' = L ⊗ π_T^*((σ^* L)⁻¹)`: its restriction along `σ` is
82	`σ^*L ⊗ σ^*(π_T^*(σ^*L)⁻¹) ≅ σ^*L ⊗ (σ^*L)⁻¹ ≅ 𝒪_T`
83	(using the section base-change iso `sectionPullbackProjIso`), and `L' ≅ π_T^*((σ^*L)⁻¹) ⊗ L`
84	differs from `L` by a pullback from the base, hence `[L'] = [L]` in
85	`Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`. -/
86	theorem exists_rigidification_relPicRel {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
87	    (σ : T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT)
88	    (hσ : σ ≫ Limits.pullback.snd πC πT = 𝟙 T) (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) :
89	    ∃ L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT,
90	      Nonempty (Rigidification σ L') ∧ PicSharp.relPicRel πC πT L' L := by
91	  classical
92	  -- `σ^* L` is locally trivial (pullback of a line bundle is a line bundle, 01HH).
93	  have hσL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial ((Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj L.carrier) :=
94	    L.isLocallyTrivial.pullback σ
95	  -- Its tensor inverse `Ninv` on `T`, with `eN : σ^* L ⊗ Ninv ≅ 𝒪_T`.
96	  obtain ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨eN⟩⟩ := Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse hσL
97	  -- The twist `L' := L ⊗ π_T^* Ninv`.
98	  refine ⟨⟨Modules.tensorObj L.carrier
99	      (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier,
100	      Modules.tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial L.isLocallyTrivial
101	        (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).isLocallyTrivial⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
102	  · -- Rigidification of `L'`:
103	    -- `σ^*(L ⊗ π_T^*Ninv) ≅ σ^*L ⊗ σ^*(π_T^*Ninv) ≅ σ^*L ⊗ Ninv ≅ 𝒪_T`.
104	    exact ⟨⟨Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial σ L.carrier
105	          (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier
106	          L.isLocallyTrivial
107	          (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).isLocallyTrivial ≪≫
108	        Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) (sectionPullbackProjIso σ hσ Ninv) ≪≫ eN⟩⟩
109	  · -- `H_T`-equivalence `L' ~ L`: `L' = L ⊗ π_T^*Ninv ≅ π_T^*Ninv ⊗ L` (braiding), take `N = Ninv`.
110	    exact ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨Modules.tensorObj_braiding L.carrier
111	      (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier⟩⟩
112	
113	/-! ## §4. The section attached to a rational point -/
114	
115	/-- **The section of the projection produced by a rational point.** A `k`-rational
116	point `x₀ : Spec k ⟶ C` (a section of the structure map `πC`) determines, for every
117	test object `T` with structure map `πT : T ⟶ S`, a section
118	`σ_T := ⟨π_T ≫ x₀, 𝟙_T⟩ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` of the projection `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`.
119	This is the section along which the relative Picard functor is rigidified. -/
120	noncomputable def rationalPointSection {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} (πT : T ⟶ S)
121	    (x₀ : S ⟶ C) (hx₀ : x₀ ≫ πC = 𝟙 S) :
122	    T ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT :=
123	  Limits.pullback.lift (πT ≫ x₀) (𝟙 T)
124	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hx₀, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp])
125	
126	@[simp]
127	theorem rationalPointSection_comp_snd {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} (πT : T ⟶ S)
128	    (x₀ : S ⟶ C) (hx₀ : x₀ ≫ πC = 𝟙 S) :
129	    rationalPointSection πT x₀ hx₀ ≫ Limits.pullback.snd πC πT = 𝟙 T :=
130	  Limits.pullback.lift_snd _ _ _
131	
132	end PicSharp
133	
134	end Scheme
